goal: Reduce native IQ1_S float dot latency at width 5120 beyond the incumbent (two independent accumulators, PR #71), one falsifiable small mechanism per attempt.
constraints: Keep packed weight decoding and float activations unchanged. No per-call heap allocation.
The incumbent already splits the native float accumulator by l&1; do not re-add accumulators or merely hoist broadcasts the compiler already hoists.
Only edit the native dot core; keep scalar fallback, public interface, tests and tolerances unchanged.
Kernel-only experiment; full-model quality, memory and speed gates plus C++ review are required before model promotion.
hints: Seek a distinct mechanism from the incumbent: for example process two 32-element groups per iteration so more independent grid loads are in flight before their FMAs, or reorder the group loop to expose more independent work. Use only small exact edits and retain generic compilation and scalar behavior.
Use compiler and test feedback. If an attempt is slower or equal, say what limited it (loads, FMA latency, decode) before proposing the next mechanism.
